applies_why: The judge labels the issue UNDERDETERMINED because paternity lacks explicit textual resolution, which is the sort of single-verse silence ground the rule governs.
quote: D6 vs C4 (Romans 1:3): UNDERDETERMINED -- answered in [CR2] section A.1-2 and [CR3] Link 6 premises 1-3, where descent according to the flesh is weighed against conception of the Holy Ghost without explicit textual resolution of paternity.
rule_words: That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side. A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand.
room: Phrase: a single verse does not state a link or its contrary. Read narrowly to bar only one verse's silence as a standalone ground; read broadly to bar lack of explicit textual resolution as a ground. The judge treats lack of explicit resolution as UNDERDETERMINED.
why: The judge's UNDERDETERMINED label depends on lack of explicit textual resolution of paternity, which K-S2 forbids as a ground.
